package_info.why_malicious: The package was compromised by a malicious developer who embedded JavaScript code in the user interface to exfiltrate users’ private deposit notes to an unauthorized external server, enabling theft of funds from users of the decentralized finance platform.

execution_context.file_location: JavaScript frontend code (likely in main UI logic or deposit/withdrawal modules)
required_permissions: access to in-browser sensitive data (deposit notes)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code accesses the user's private deposit note and sends its value to an external attacker-controlled server via HTTPS POST, enabling exfiltration of sensitive credentials.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exfiltrating private deposit notes to an external server is a clear violation of user privacy and security, as these notes are the cryptographic keys required to withdraw funds from the mixer.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Tornado Cash UI code should never transmit private deposit notes or secrets to any external server; all cryptographic operations should be local and privacy-preserving.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or error reporting might send non-sensitive usage data, but never private cryptographic secrets.
key_indicators: Access to sensitive in-browser data (deposit notes)
Network request to non-official, attacker-controlled domain
No user consent or notification for data exfiltration

attack_chain.action: Malicious developer commits JavaScript code to the Tornado Cash UI repository.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is deployed to the production UI.

attack_chain.action: User interacts with the compromised Tornado Cash UI and generates a private deposit note.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes in the user's browser.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code captures the user's private deposit note and sends it to the attacker's server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives deposit notes and can steal funds.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses stolen deposit notes to withdraw funds from Tornado Cash, draining user accounts.
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: theft of user funds.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code accessing in-browser cryptographic secrets (deposit notes)
Network requests from UI to non-official, external domains during sensitive operations
Unexpected POST requests containing deposit notes or private keys
file_indicators: Modifications to main UI JavaScript files handling deposit/withdrawal logic
New or altered code referencing external domains not associated with the project
network_indicators: HTTPS POST requests to attacker-controlled domains (not tornado.cash or official infrastructure)
Unusual outbound traffic from user browsers during deposit/withdrawal
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor the Tornado Cash UI codebase for unauthorized changes that access and transmit deposit notes or other secrets. Use browser extension or proxy tools to detect POST requests from the UI to non-official domains, especially during deposit or withdrawal operations. Audit JavaScript code for any logic that serializes and sends sensitive data externally. Alert on any network activity from the UI to domains not on an allowlist.
